question: [FREE] Based on the video clip, what probe adjustment is performed after the initial landmark is identified, and what view is it intended to bring into frame?
answer: The operator tilts/angles the probe toward the feet to bring the uterus into view and, if present, identify the fetus within it.
groundtruth: After identifying the bladder, the operator tilts the transducer toward the feet to bring the uterus into view and ideally visualize a fetus within it.

question: [FREE] Based on the video clip, what part of the overall workflow is being set up, and what imaging condition must be achieved before placing measurement markers?
answer: They are setting up for the first-trimester dating measurement (CRL). Before placing markers, they optimize the plane by elongating the fetal view and adjusting until the true long axis/maximal end-to-end length is captured.
groundtruth: The operator transitions into crown–rump length measurement setup and manipulates the probe to elongate the fetal view, then fans/rotates to ensure the true longitudinal axis and maximal crown–rump distance are captured before measuring.

question: [FREE] This clip shows the target not yet displayed at its maximal end-to-end span. What optimization maneuver is performed, and why does it matter?
answer: The probe is maneuvered to elongate the fetal view so the maximal crown-to-rump distance is shown, reducing foreshortening and improving measurement accuracy.
groundtruth: The operator adjusts probe position/angle to elongate the fetal view to obtain the maximal crown–rump distance for an accurate CRL measurement.

question: [FREE] Based on the video clip, what machine interaction is performed to refine the chosen image for measurement, and why is it used?
answer: The operator freezes the live scan and then scrolls/cines through the saved frames to select the single frame that best shows the fetal poles for accurate measurement.
groundtruth: The scan is frozen and cine review is used to move back through frames to choose the best frame demonstrating the optimal pole-to-pole view for measurement.
